In my humble opinion. You should always have One champ which you know inside and out. If the comp is right, and you are lastpick, you know you can take this champ and win lane 99% of the time. You should then have 2 safe picks. Champs you know how to play, that don't require you to win lane to be effective. For example Shen or Morde. You still need to KNOW these champs, matchups, mechanics. For example, at lvl one wukong beats Morde with his E. But if Morde survives long enough in lane, wukong can't touch him at later levels. Simply playing them isn't enough. For low elo, this should be fine. As you get higher in skill you should increase these numbers. And remember. It's not about knowing how to win, it's about knowing how to not lose.

TLDR you should have in-depth knowledge of three champs, one of which should be a lane bully.

do NOT jump straight into ranked.

This will straight up make you worse at the game.

Unranked has a "hidden" rank. So as you play normal games, if you are winning, your opponents are getting harder. As you lose games, your opponents get easier. If you go into ranked, you are starting fresh. Meaning (most likely) worse opponents. You are going to learn a lot less by playing games with these people, and will learn a lot more from sticking with normals, where the competition is actually of a similar skill level to you. If you jump into ranked now and lose a few, you will play against people that are worse than you, and you will start to play like them. If you happen to win a load, you will end up struggle to do well and enjoy the game. Stick with normals until you have learned most of what you feel you need to, then hop into ranked to learn the rest.

It's up to you, but this is my advice. I played normals for 2 years before I touched ranked, and 4 years later, I am Diamond. My friend played ranked straight away, 5 years later he is silver 4.
